The Islamic year is 354/355 days, so the Gregorian-365 framing is itself a critique point (WikiIslam).

verification_scholar_rule.note: Stated rule verified: singular yawm without suffixes = 365 (simple يوم/اليوم/يوما 274 + prefixed ويوم 44, واليوم 23, ليوم 8, فاليوم 8, بيوم 5, باليوم 2, وباليوم 1). QAC agrees: singular yawm = 375, minus 10 suffixed = 365.

findings.scholar_method: Yahya's page states the qualifier: 'The word faith (iman) (without genitive) is repeated 25 times throughout the Qur'an as is also the word infidelity (kufr).' Units: the nouns إيمان / كفر, with the genitive excluded. What '(without genitive)' means in practice is reconstructed below (see verification note); the qualifier itself is verbatim from the source.
findings.exceptions: Genitive in Arabic covers the possessive pronoun suffixes (إيمانهم/إيمانكم/كفرهم -- the suffix is a genitive pronoun). Bare (unsuffixed) tokens: iman 25 (GEN-case 12 + ACC-case 11 + NOM-case 2); kufr 25 (ACC-case 14 + GEN-case 10 + NOM-case 1). Suffixed tokens excluded: iman 20, kufr 12. The alternative reading -- excluding all GEN-case tokens -- gives 21 (iman) and 20 (kufr) and does NOT reproduce 25. The circulating list (quranic-miracles.com) gives iman/kufr as 17, not 25.

verification_scholar_rule.note: Reconstructed implementation of the stated qualifier: bare (unsuffixed) noun forms give exactly 25/25 (QAC LEM <iyma`n bare 25; LEM kufor bare 25). Both words occur together in several of the same verses (2:108, 3:167, 3:177, 9:23, 16:106, 49:7).

verification_root_rule.note: QAC noun-only (root narrowed by lemma to the intended sense): LEM <iyma`n = 45, LEM kufor = 37. The 25/25 is the bare-noun subset. Broader sense-level families: belief (verb آمن 537 + مؤمن 202 + إيمان 45 + مؤمنات 22 + مؤمنة 6) = 812; disbelief (ROOT kfr minus كفّارة 'expiation') = 507.

correction.why: Yahya's '(without genitive)' reproduces exactly once it is read as 'without the genitive/possessive pronominal suffixes': bare إيمان = 25 and bare كفر = 25 (QAC, script-counted, both sides). The filed note said no clean rule reproduces 25/25; the bare-form rule does, on both sides at once.
